also: it depends a lot on whether

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation: with ex and the ablative
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.107: ex quō verbō … tōta illa causa pendēbat
terms.comment: What a thing depends on goes in ex with the ablative; Lewis & Short also give in, ab, dē or the plain ablative. Of people: tuōrum, quī ex tē pendent, your family, who depend on you (Cic. Fam. 6.22.2).

terms.gloss: depend on someone, be up to someone
terms.grammar: phrase: in with the ablative; positum agrees with what depends
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.25.3: id ille in tē positum esse putat
Traupman 96: tōtum in tē positum est, it all depends on you
terms.comment: Also of the self: ut omnia tua in tē posita esse dūcās, that you think everything that is yours depends on yourself (Cic. Lael. 7).

terms.gloss: it depends (who, what, how, whether …); it makes a difference
terms.grammar: impersonal verb (from intersum): with an indirect question
evidence: Plin. Ep. 6.24.1: Quam multum interest quid ā quōque fīat!
Cic. Fam. 13.10.4: interest quālis prīmus aditus sit
terms.comment: “It depends” is a construction of its own: interest or rēfert, it matters, with an indirect question, its verb in the subjunctive. Traupman (p. 96) gives plūrimum rēfert num …, it depends a lot on whether …. That it makes no difference is nihil interest, nīl rēfert (see it makes no difference).

phrases.latin: cui spēs omnis et ratiō et cōgitātiō pendet ex fortūnā, huic nihil potest esse certī
phrases.english: a man whose every hope, plan and thought depends on fortune can be sure of nothing

phrases.latin: id ille in tē positum esse putat mihique persuādet
phrases.english: he thinks it depends on you, and he has convinced me

phrases.latin: Quam multum interest quid ā quōque fīat!
phrases.english: How much depends on who does a thing!

phrases.latin: sīc ignis nōn rēfert quam magnus sed quō incidat
phrases.english: so with a fire, it depends not on how big it is but on where it falls

phrases.latin: prout locus inīquus aequusve hīs aut illīs, prout animus pugnantium est, prout numerus …, varia fortūna pugnae est
phrases.english: depending on whether the ground favoured one side or the other, on the fighters’ spirit and on their numbers, the fortune of the fight varied
It depends a lot on whether …
